tools.title: Blueprint Assist
tools.summary: Automatic Blueprint graph formatting plus keyboard-first node navigation and editing.
workflow: Install the compatible plugin build.
Share team settings through source control.
Format after meaningful graph changes, not on every tiny operation.
Use it as presentation/readability tooling, not architecture.
tools.codex: After Codex mutates a graph, a formatter integration could normalize node layout before review.
tools.caution: Formatting cannot fix bad responsibilities or coupling. Keep architecture rules separate.

tools.title: Auto Size Comments
tools.summary: Automatically keeps Blueprint comment boxes sized around their nodes and supports comment style presets.
workflow: Install into the project/engine plugin folder.
Use consistent comment presets.
Group logic by responsibility, not by arbitrary screen region.
Review graph-specific compatibility.
tools.codex: Codex can preserve comments and create meaningful graph sections; this plugin keeps the visual grouping tidy.
tools.caution: Some graph types have compatibility limitations; verify on the target UE version.

tools.title: Electronic Nodes
tools.summary: Alternative wire rendering for Blueprint, Material and other graph editors.
workflow: Install only if a UE 5.8-compatible build is available.
Choose one team-wide wire style.
Do not make screenshots/reviews depend on personal-only styling.
tools.codex: No direct automation value; improves human review of graphs generated or edited by Codex.
tools.caution: The public compatibility table currently documents up to UE 5.7; verify before adopting on 5.8.

tools.title: Blueprint Diff
tools.summary: Unreal's asset-aware diff workflow for comparing Blueprint revisions instead of treating .uasset files as opaque binaries.
workflow: Compare the working Blueprint against the previous revision.
Review graph, defaults and component changes.
Reject unexpected changes before save/commit.
Capture diff evidence in PRs for important assets.
tools.codex: Use as a human/automation verification concept: re-read changed graphs and surface a semantic summary before commit.
tools.caution: Git textual diff is not meaningful for .uasset files; use Unreal-aware diffing.

tools.title: BlueprintUE
tools.summary: Plugin/service workflow for sharing Blueprint graphs in a web-readable format.
why: Good for bug reports and design review
workflow: Use only for non-sensitive graphs.
Export/share the smallest relevant graph.
Keep source-of-truth in the Unreal project.
Do not upload proprietary logic without approval.
tools.codex: Useful for sharing a graph snapshot with humans; not required for internal MCP editing.
tools.caution: External service and documented plugin compatibility must be reviewed before project use.

tools.title: RyHelpfulHelpers
tools.summary: Large helper plugin exposing runtime/editor utilities for Blueprints and C++.
workflow: Audit only the helpers you would actually use.
Avoid taking a large dependency for one trivial helper.
Prefer engine-native APIs when equivalent.
Wrap adopted helpers behind project abstractions if they become core.
tools.codex: Reference source for missing utility functions; can reduce generated boilerplate.
tools.caution: Broad helper libraries can become dependency magnets; evaluate footprint and ownership.

tools.title: Blueprint Console Commands
tools.summary: Makes it easy to expose Blueprint functions as developer console/cheat commands.
workflow: Keep commands development-only.
Group commands by system.
Use commands to reproduce states quickly.
Pair with automation tests where a scenario becomes stable.
tools.codex: Codex can call documented console commands during PIE debugging or generate new debug-only commands.
tools.caution: Never expose privileged/debug commands in shipping builds unintentionally.

tools.title: Quick Actions
tools.summary: Open-source Unreal editor productivity plugin from Out-of-the-Box Plugins.
why: Good source of reusable editor extension patterns
Potential replacement for one-off repetitive editor actions
workflow: Review current feature list against your workflow.
Adopt only actions that save repeated manual work.
Keep project-critical automation in our own toolset or official APIs.
tools.codex: Potential human productivity companion; source also provides editor-extension implementation examples.
tools.caution: Treat as optional convenience, not a required project dependency.

tools.title: FlowGraph
tools.summary: Design-agnostic async node graph for game flow, quests, sequences and narrative scripting.
workflow: Use when the game has substantial quest/narrative/event flow.
Build project-specific Flow nodes.
Keep low-level gameplay inside components/systems.
Use FlowGraph to orchestrate, not own every gameplay detail.
tools.codex: Codex can help author custom flow nodes and inspect flow assets once we expose dedicated readers.
tools.caution: Adds a major architectural abstraction; adopt intentionally, not for tiny projects.

tools.title: Blueprint Header View
tools.summary: Previews a Blueprint class or struct as C++-style declarations for variables, functions, components and dispatchers.
why: Makes Blueprint structure easier to understand from code-oriented workflows
Useful context for Codex before creating equivalent C++ types
Highlights class shape without manually reading every graph
workflow: Right-click a Blueprint class or struct.
Choose Preview Equivalent C++ Header.
Review variables, functions, components and event dispatchers.
Use the preview as migration/design context; implement actual function logic manually in C++.
tools.codex: Use as supporting evidence when deciding whether a Blueprint should remain visual scripting or move behind a C++ API.
tools.caution: This produces declarations, not a complete automatic Blueprint-to-C++ conversion.
